blocks.text: Wesgro is accountable for twelve initiatives and does part of the work in all eighteen; for the other six, the accountable lead sits with another tier, and the plan names it.

The matrix below assigns each initiative to the four roles: responsible (R) for doing the work, accountable (A) for the result, consulted (C) before decisions and informed (I) of progress. Where Wesgro is accountable and does the work itself, the cell reads A/R. Assignments are proposals for Steerco to confirm, built from the actions in Chapter 3.

blocks.text: National government and the state-owned entities

Four levers sit outside the province and cannot be bought or marketed into place. Route rights and visas sit with the national tier (Current State Diagnostic, Dec 2025, p58), the airport and port capital programmes with national SOEs (Infrastructure Report, Jul 2026, p103, p112) and policing with SAPS. The plan treats them as an escalation agenda (I17), carried by Steerco through DEDAT to the national departments and SOEs. Each item is stated as a decision, an owner and a date the province is asking for. Wesgro's own route work (I6) runs inside the existing agreements meanwhile.

DEDAT is a standing member of Steerco and the accountable lead where the lever is policy or funding rather than promotion: quality standards (I10), LTO funding and climate risk (I13) and the labour analysis (I18). The Department of Mobility leads the transport half of corridor mobility (I8). Wesgro's units lead the demand, access, product and data initiatives and report through the programme office.

Municipalities and LTOs hold the assets, the selling bodies and the visitor services that the regional and inclusion initiatives depend on. They lead the community selling bodies in the pilots (I12), attach covenants to public assets (I12, I14) and carry the route and product work in their districts (I3, I9). The City of Cape Town and Cape Town Tourism are partners on events, mobility and data (I2, I8, I16) and sit on Steerco.
The private sector and site operators

Airlines decide frequency and gauge, hotel investors decide the mid-scale tier and attraction operators manage their own capacity. The plan gives them the evidence and the demand case. It asks for the decisions it cannot make for them: seats on full routes (I6), investment in secondary nodes (I14) and visitor-flow management at flagship sites, where the operators are accountable (I11).
